_status: LIVE — classification verified, known bugs documented, pipeline run 2026-03-31
_coverage_rationale: REF-DEAL-RE-1: Real estate preferred equity / CRE construction offering memorandum. Cross Development + Nobis Rehabilitation Partners building a 48-bed Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility in Albuquerque, NM. Tests that the system correctly identifies the real estate archetype at the worker layer, documents the known limitation that 'real_estate' is not an expressible deal_type in the core context enum, and guards against revenue noise from construction budget line items.
_failure_modes_targeted: BUG-RE-1: 'real_estate' is not in DIOContext.deal_type enum — real estate deals collapse to fund_spv via deterministic realAsset override in packages/core/src/orchestration/dio-context.ts lines ~1036-1069

BUG-RE-2: structured_summary.kpis.raise = $35.6M (construction loan) instead of $11.9M (equity raise) — the first large dollar figure in the exec summary context is the construction loan, not the equity offering
Revenue noise BUG-RE-3: 'Gross Receipt Sales Tax $2,352,769' on construction budget page extracted as Revenue $2,352,769B — scale corruption causing a cents amount to read as $2.35 quadrillion
Business model noise BUG-RE-4: deal_summary_v1.one_liner = 'Omnichannel (DTC + Wholesale/Retail)' — completely inapplicable to a CRE construction preferred equity deal
_known_limitation: BUG-RE-1 is a SYSTEMIC LIMITATION. The DIOContext deal_type enum does not include 'real_estate' or 'real_estate_preferred_equity'. The deterministic realAsset override intentionally routes all CRE deals to deal_type=fund_spv as the nearest approximation. The fix requires extending the enum and adding a real_estate routing path. Until fixed, report_checks assert fund_spv as EXPECTED CURRENT BEHAVIOR — not correctness.

slots.company_description: Cross Development and Kennor Holdings ('Cross' or 'Sponsor') are seeking preferred equity investors for the development of a 48-bed, 52,381 sq. ft. Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) in Albuquerque, NM. The property is 100% leased to Albuquerque Rehabilitation Hospital LLC, an entity owned by Nobis Rehabilitation Partners, which operates 16 IRF hospitals nationwide. This is the 9th development in the Cross + Nobis build-to-suit partnership.
slots.deal_structure: Preferred equity construction opportunity. Capital stack: $35.6M construction loan (75% LTC) + $11.9M equity ($8.9M preferred equity + $2.97M sponsor). Total project cost $47.5M. Preferred equity returns 15% IRR guaranteed. Exit cap rate 7.0% vs build-to cap rate 10.0%.
slots.product_type: Real estate — CRE construction / build-to-suit single-tenant healthcare facility
slots.asset_class: Commercial real estate — Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF), healthcare net lease
slots.lease_structure: 20-year NNN (Absolute Triple-Net), 1.5% annual escalations, two 5-year renewal options. No landlord obligations.
slots.deal_type_context_note: BUG-RE-1: context.deal_type = fund_spv is the CURRENT SYSTEM OUTPUT, not the correct classification. Worker-layer correctly identifies as real_estate / real_estate_preferred_equity. Fix requires adding real_estate to DIOContext enum.
slots.document_title: Albuquerque, NM - Nobis Pref. Equity Opportunity.pdf

financials._note: This is a CRE construction offering memorandum — not a startup financial package. The document contains a project budget, DSCR projections, and NOI analysis — NOT operating company P&L. financial_breakdown_v1 erroneously models this as a startup-style financial package. Core financial data points are the construction capital stack and projected NOI, not revenue/burn/cash.

current_state._note: No operating company financials. financial_breakdown_v1.current_state.data_quality = 'partial' (noise-driven — $2.35 quadrillion revenue from BUG-RE-3). True current-state operating data does not apply here; only the construction capital stack matters.

construction_loan.evidence: Executive summary: 'Cross is seeking a 75% LTC construction loan in the amount of $35,605,000'

equity_raise.evidence: Executive summary: 'Cross will raise an additional $11,868,000 as equity to complete the capital stack'

total_project_cost.evidence: Executive summary: 'Total Project Cost $47.5M' / budget page total uses = $47,473,000

noi_year1.evidence: Executive summary: 'The Year 1 net operating income of the asset will be $4,747,300'

preferred_equity_irr.evidence: Executive summary: 'The Preferred Equity will receive a guaranteed 15% IRR for their investment'

revenue_scale_corruption_BUG_RE_3.evidence: The construction budget page (Sources & Uses) contains 'Gross Receipt Sales Tax $2,352,769'. The extraction reads '$2,352,769B' (where B comes from trailing 'Bank' OCR artifact or unit misparse), then stores $2,352,769 * 10^9. This is a tax line item in a construction budget, not operating revenue. True revenue for this deal is not meaningful — the 'revenue' is really NOI/lease income.

raise_amount_wrong_BUG_RE_2.evidence: structured_summary.kpis.raise = '$35.6M Equity' (amount: $35,605,000) — this is the CONSTRUCTION LOAN, not the equity offering. The executive summary mentions $35.6M first in 'construction loan ... $35,605,000' context. The actual equity raise being offered to investors is $11,868,000 ($8.9M preferred equity + $2.97M sponsor). The financial_facts_v1 table correctly stores $11,900,000 (raise_amount, high confidence, pdf_kpi_line).

business_model_misclassification_BUG_RE_.correct_value: Real estate structured investment (construction preferred equity)
business_model_misclassification_BUG_RE_.evidence: deal_summary_v1.one_liner = 'Omnichannel (DTC + Wholesale/Retail)' — completely inapplicable to a CRE deal. The business_model_signal_v1 pattern never ran a real-estate-aware path. deal_overview_v2.business_model correctly returns 'Real estate structured investment'.

extraction_checks.note: The $11.9M equity raise is correctly stored in financial_facts_v1 (raise_amount, high confidence, Q1 2026). This tests that the fact storage layer captures the equity figure even though the structured_summary layer picks up the wrong (construction loan) figure.

noise_checks.label: Revenue must not be >= $1T (construction budget sales tax noise)
noise_checks.note: BUG-RE-3 guard: 'Gross Receipt Sales Tax $2,352,769' extracted as $2,352,769B ($2.35 quadrillion). Any revenue fact >= $1T for this deal is noise. Revenue in this context is NOI ($4.7M), not a billion-scale figure.

noise_checks.label: financial_breakdown revenue must not be >= $1B
noise_checks.note: BUG-RE-3: financial_breakdown_v1.current_state.revenue.value = 2352769000000000 is a known regression. Any value >= $1B for this deal's revenue is noise.

report_checks.label: deal_type context must be fund_spv (known limitation BUG-RE-1)
report_checks.note: EXPECTED CURRENT BEHAVIOR (BUG-RE-1). The correct value should be 'real_estate_preferred_equity' but is not expressible in the current enum. If this check FAILS, it means someone changed the real-asset routing — verify whether the new behavior is better or a regression.

report_checks.label: primary_doc_type must be business_plan_im (real-asset routing applied)
report_checks.note: Deterministic real-asset routing in dio-context.ts sets primary_doc_type = 'business_plan_im' for real estate preferred equity deals. This confirms the routing fired.

report_checks.label: stage must be fund_ops (real-asset routing applied)
report_checks.note: Real-asset routing sets stage = 'fund_ops'. If this regresses to 'seed' or 'series_a', the deterministic override stopped firing.

dio_checks.label: business_archetype_v1 must be real_estate
dio_checks.note: CORRECT CLASSIFICATION at the worker layer. The archetype classifier correctly identifies real_estate via re:real_estate (cap rate, preferred equity) and re:noicap (cap rate language) rules. If this regresses to 'unknown', the real_estate archetype rules need to be re-added.

dio_checks.label: business_archetype_v1 confidence must be >= 0.5
dio_checks.note: Confidence was 0.60 at time of GT creation.

dio_checks.label: deal_overview_v2 deal_type must be real_estate_preferred_equity
dio_checks.note: CORRECT CLASSIFICATION at the worker layer. deal_overview_v2 uses the worker's own classifier which correctly identifies CRE preferred equity deals. This is the truth signal that should eventually be promoted to context.deal_type.

dio_checks.label: deal_overview_v2 business_model must be Real estate structured investment
dio_checks.note: Worker correctly returns 'Real estate structured investment'. Guards against regression to startup-style business model labels.

evidence_checks.label: real_estate archetype evidence must include re:real_estate rule
evidence_checks.note: re:real_estate rule (preferred equity, cap rate signals) is the primary trigger for the real_estate archetype.

evidence_checks.label: real_estate archetype evidence must include re:noicap rule
evidence_checks.note: re:noicap rule fires on cap rate / NOI language in the document.
